To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) double integrating sphere method is fast and comparable to single integrating sphere method in measuring reflectance spectra; (ii) transmittance spectra obtained with double integrating sphere method are different compared to single integrating spheres; (iii) leaf clip method is fast but not comparable to integrating spheres in measuring leaf spectra; and (iv) differences between methods are larger in transmittance than in reflectance.
the three methods are comparable in terms of within-method variability, and the differences between methods are small for reflectance but large for transmittance.

(1) the leaf reflectance spectra measured with a small double integrating spheres are comparable to those measured with a large integrating spheres; (2) the leaf reflectances measured with leaf clips are higher than those measured with a single integrating sphere, and (3) the leaf transmittance measured with a small integrating sphere is higher than that measured with a single sphere, which may be due to the different illumination conditions.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the accuracy and applicability of methods for measuring leaf reflectance and transmission spectra, which are important for remote sensing and modeling of energy budgets of vegetation.
methods for measuring leaf reflectance and transmission.
the development of methods for fast, portable, and accurate acquisition of leaf spectra.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
all methods are useful, but they should be used with care, and the differences between methods should be taken into account in data analysis.
all methods are suitable for leaf reflectance and/or transmittance measurements, but that the choice of the method should be based on the purpose of the measurements.

the three methods can be used to measure leaf reflectance and/or transmittance spectra with comparable accuracy, provided that the measurements are made under the same conditions and the same target is measured.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the double integrating sphere and the leaf clip are suitable for measuring reflectance spectra, whereas the leaf clip is also suitable for transmittance measurements.
all methods are suitable for measuring leaf reflectance and leaf transmittance spectra, if the differences between methods are taken into account.
the single and double integrating sphere methods are comparable in accuracy, whereas leaf clip is slightly less accurate.
The main takeaway from our work is that

leaf reflectance and especially transmittance spectra measured with double integrating sphere and leaf clip are comparable to those measured with conventional single integrating sphere, and that the double integrating sphere is the most practical of the three methods.
it is important to be aware of potential differences between the methods, and to use the same method in all measurements.
it is not sufficient to measure leaf reflectance and/or transmittance with only one of the methods.
